summary: Jeskola Bass 3's line plays on Neo Poly as a mono legato bass: notes as notes (in its pitch convention), slides as glides, volume as velocity; cutoff, resonance and waveform carry over.

rules.why: assumed: 100 % moves the cutoff 3 octaves (F1 env +50 %)
noise has no oscillator shape on Neo Poly (its Noise level is a separate source): left as it was

notes.why: Each row's note lasts to the track's next note (or Note lenght ticks); Slide note glides to it over the note; Volume (0x80 = 100 %) is the velocity, 0x80 → 64, with Vel → amp at 100 % and Volume +6 dB making up for it.

remarks: No new machine (machine-safety.md §4, H4): Neo Poly in Legato with glide plays the bass line; its ladder filter and envelopes take the cutoff, resonance and envelope settings.

The cutoff and envelope scales are assumed (closed source: the texts are bare 0–100 % or 0–128): a cutoff of 0 % is laid on 80 Hz and 100 % on 16 kHz, logarithmically; the timbres differ, the notes, their lengths, slides and loudness carry over.
Each Jeskola Bass 3 track is its own voice with its own filter; Neo Poly in Legato is one voice with one filter: a song playing several tracks at once needs Voice mode Poly after the move.

tolerance.why_not: Not measured per band: the filters and oscillators are different models and the closed machines' cutoff and envelope scales are unmeasured, so the timbre differs; loudness is matched (the output gain) and checked.

evidence: ExternalMachines/source/buzztrax-buzzmachines/CyanPhase/DTMF/CyanPhase_DTMF-1_Demo.bmx and Jeskola/Ninja/Jeskola_NiNjA_dElaY.bmx: its parameter table (Volume 1–254, Note lenght 1–255, Slide note)
